{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2018}}
'''Justin Tatch Moore''' (born 1974)<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |url=https://settheory.mathtalks.org/speaker/justin-moore/ |title=Set Theory Talks Global set theory seminar and conference announcements (Moore's short biography) |access-date=13 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707123921/https://settheory.mathtalks.org/speaker/justin-moore/ |archive-date=7 July 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> is a set theorist and logician. He is a full professor in mathematics at [[Cornell University]]. 

==Career==
Moore received his PhD in 2000 from the [[University of Toronto]] under the supervision of [[Stevo Todorcevic]].<ref name="bio"/><ref name="Genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46051_2020-08-26">{{Citation | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46051| title=Justin Moore - The Mathematics Genealogy Project| newspaper=Genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46051| access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref> He was an assistant professor in mathematics at [[Boise State University]]. In the fall of 2007, he joined the faculty at [[Cornell University]].

==Research== 
His primary research area is [[Ramsey theory]] of infinite sets. He is known for solutions to the basis problem for uncountable linear orders and to the L space problem from [[general topology]]<ref>Justin Tatch Moore: A SOLUTION TO THE L SPACE PROBLEM, JOURNAL OF THE AMERICAN MATHEMATICAL SOCIETY Volume 19, Number 3, Pages 717–736 [https://www.ams.org/journals/jams/2006-19-03/S0894-0347-05-00517-5/S0894-0347-05-00517-5.pdf]</ref> and for his work in determining the consequences of relating the continuum to certain values of the [http://www.mathreference.com/set-card,aleph.html aleph function].<ref name="Pi.math.cornell.edu/~justin/_2020-08-26">{{Citation | url=https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~justin/| title=Justin Tatch Moore's Home Page| newspaper=Pi.math.cornell.edu/~justin/| access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref> Moore, together with his PhD student Yash Lodha, produced the first torsion-free and finitely presented counterexample to the [[Von Neumann conjecture|von Neumann-Day problem]], originally described by mathematician [[John von Neumann]] in 1929. Lodha presented this solution at the London Mathematical Society's Geometric and Cohomological Group Theory symposium in August 2013.<ref>[https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/11/131118133041.htm  Vasyl Kacapyr: Von Neumann-Day problem: Vexing math problem finds an elegant solution,  Science Daily, November 18, 2013 ]</ref>

==Awards, distinctions, and recognitions==
Moore won the "Young Scholar's Competition" award in 2006, in Vienna, Austria. The Competition was a part of the "Horizons of Truth" celebrating the Gödel Centenary 2006.<ref name="Robert.barringtonleigh.net_2020-08-26">{{Citation | url=https://robert.barringtonleigh.net/biography/UTorontoMathDepartment-March2007.pdf| title=University of Toronto, Department of Mathematics: Outstanding award for Justin Moore| newspaper=Robert.barringtonleigh.net| access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref> He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]], [[Hyderabad]] 2010, Logic session, where he presented his solution to the problem of constructing an L-space. The L-space was constructed without assuming additional axioms and by combining Todorcevic's rho functions with number theory.<ref name="Web.archive.org_2020-08-26">{{Citation | url=https://rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/candidates/TODORCEVIC%2C%20Stevo.pdf| title=RSC Fellowship Citation and Detailed Appraisal: Stevo Todorcevic| newspaper=Web.archive.org| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009193648/https://rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/candidates/TODORCEVIC%2C%20Stevo.pdf| access-date=26 August 2020| archive-date=9 October 2016}}</ref><ref>Bhatia, Rajendra (ed): Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Volume 1, Plenary Lectures and Ceremonies, Hyderabad 2010 p. 3</ref>

Moore is an editor for the Archive of Mathematical Logic where he handles papers in set theory.<ref name="Pi.math.cornell.edu/~justin/_2020-08-26"/> He was one of the organizers of the fall 2012 Thematic Program in Forcing and its Applications (Forcing Axioms and their Applications) at the [[Fields Institute]].<ref name="Fields.utoronto.ca/programs/scientific/12-13/forcing/axioms/index.html_2020-08-26">{{Citation | url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/programs/scientific/12-13/forcing/axioms/index.html| title=Fields Institute - Workshop on Forcing axioms and their applications| newspaper=Fields.utoronto.ca/programs/scientific/12-13/forcing/axioms/index.html| access-date=26 August 2020}}</ref>
In 2012, he was elected as a Fellow (Inaugural Class of Fellows) of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]. Retrieved 5 March 2018</ref>
